Boris Godunov. Modest Mussorgsky's Boris Godunov, composed in 1874, is a monumental Russian opera based on Alexander Pushkin's historical drama and Nikolay Karamzin's history. Set during the chaotic Time of Troubles, from 1598 to 1605, the opera tells the story of Tsar Boris Godunov, who takes the Russian throne after the mysterious assassination of the young Tsarevich Dmitry, the rightful heir of Ivan the Terrible.

Boris is the Tsar of Russia whose guilt over the murder of the child heir Dmitry leads to his descent into paranoia and final collapse. Grigori Otrepyev, known as the False Dmitry, is a young novice monk who learns of Dmitry's murder from his mentor, escapes his monastery, and claims the heir's identity to launch a rebellion supported by Poland. Pimen is an elderly monk and chronicler whose writing of Russia's history, including the murder of the Tsarevich, inadvertently inspires Grigori to impersonate the prince. Prince Shuisky is a deceptive boyar who acts as Boris's chief advisor but secretly plots to overthrow him, feeding Boris's paranoia with details of Dmitry's death. The Holy Fool, a peasant called Yurodivy, speaks truth to power and famously confronts Boris in public, refusing to pray for him because Tsar Herod murdered the young prince.

The opera begins with the Coronation Scene, a spectacular moment in the Prologue, characterized by the ringing of giant Moscow cathedral bells and Boris's solemn, foreboding prayer as he is crowned. The Clock Scene is Boris's Act Two monologue in which he hallucinates the ghost of the murdered Tsarevich, begging God for mercy while a chiming clock drives him mad. Tormented by guilt, Boris's reign is undermined by a massive famine, boyar conspiracies, and the rise of the False Dmitry. Boris is eventually driven to madness and dies, leaving Russia in political turmoil. The work is celebrated for its powerful choral writing, portraying the Russian populace as the true protagonist of the drama. Mussorgsky was a member of "The Five," a group of Russian nationalist composers of the Romantic era.
